data.content_ref: inline:CONTRADICTION: SRC_001 claims resumption is unsafe without an explicit barrier because resumed events may depend on lost causal context (working memory, attention state). This contradicts SRC_005's claim that resumption is safe whenever the partial fragment is causally inert and the resumed stream depends solely on committed events. Specifically, if the reasoning envelope has no side channels (SRC_005 countercondition), then the 'lost causal context' SRC_001 worries about was never durable and never influences the resumed stream—so resumption is safe without a barrier. The isolated problem must adjudicate this contradiction: either barriers are always necessary (SRC_001) or only necessary when side channels exist (SRC_005). REFUTED IF: stateless reasoning is shown to be impossible in practice (every reasoning step intrinsically relies on non-committed internal state that persists across interruption), which would make SRC_005's countercondition unreachable and dissolve the contradiction.
